title: CHAPTER SIX. On the grace of heavenly and holy calling: third principle defined
latin: CAPUT SEXTUM, De gratia supernae & sanctae vocationis. Sequitur gratia supernae & sanctae vocationis, quae est tertium salutis humanae principium, quo Spiritus sanctus a Patre per sacrificium Filii toti mundo placato & Filio datus omnes peccatores sine exceptione ad fidem Christi vocat & ad vitae participationem serio invitat. Hoc salutis humanae principium appellamus vocationem supernam & sanctam, cum Apostolo ad Phil. 3:14 & 2 Tim. 1:9, adeoque caelestem, Heb. 3:1, quae differt ab inferna & externa, qua quis ad functionem officii ecclesiastici aut politici legitime vocatur, ut Aaron, Exod. 28:1, & Saulus, 1 Sam. 10:1, Apostoli & in illis Judas quoque, Joh. 6:70, & personalis dici potest. Illa vero communis & spiritualis est, qua omnes homines ad communionem bonorum spiritualium vocantur.
english: CHAPTER SIX. On the grace of heavenly and holy calling.

There follows the grace of heavenly and holy calling, which is the third principle of human salvation, by which the Holy Spirit, given by the Father through the sacrifice of the Son who has propitiated the whole world, and given to the Son, calls all sinners without exception to the faith of Christ and seriously invites them to participation in life.

We call this principle of human salvation heavenly and holy calling, with the Apostle at Philippians 3:14 and 2 Timothy 1:9 — and so heavenly (Heb. 3:1) — which differs from the lower and external call by which someone is lawfully called to the function of an ecclesiastical or political office, as Aaron (Exod. 28:1) and Saul (1 Sam. 10:1), the Apostles and among them Judas also (John 6:70), and which can be called personal. But that former calling is common and spiritual, by which all humans are called to the communion of spiritual goods.

title: III–V. Parts of calling: offering of redemption-grace and precept to embrace it
latin: III. Partes sunt oblatio gratiae redemtionis & praeceptio de ea amplectenda. IV. Oblatio gratiae redemtionis est, qua Spiritus sanctus omnibus peccatoribus offerre, verbo suo offert. Sic docet Christus, Matth. 22:4,8 & seqq.; Luc. 14:17. V. Praeceptio de amplectenda redemtionis gratia est, qua Spiritus sanctus vocatos universos serio jubet oblatam redemtionis gratiam in Christo acceptare, eaque ad salutem suam frui. Sic docet Christus Luc. 14:23 & Paulus 2 Cor. 5:20; 1 Tim. 2:4.
english: III. The parts are the offering of the grace of redemption and the precept concerning embracing it.
IV. The offering of the grace of redemption is that by which the Holy Spirit offers to all sinners, by His word. So Christ teaches (Matt. 22:4,8 and following; Luke 14:17).

V. The precept concerning embracing the grace of redemption is that by which the Holy Spirit seriously commands all the called to accept the offered grace of redemption in Christ and to enjoy it for their salvation. So Christ teaches (Luke 14:23) and Paul (2 Cor. 5:20; 1 Tim. 2:4).
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Ye parts stand as ye offering belonging toward ye grace belonging toward redemption and ye precept concerning embracing it. — III. — Luke 14:17). — 22:4,8 and following; — So Christ teaches (Matt. — Ye offering belonging toward ye grace belonging toward redemption stands as that by which ye Holy Spirit offers toward all sinners, by His word. — IV. — 2:4). — 1 Tim. — 5:20; — So Christ teaches (Luke 14:23) and Paul (2 Cor. — Ye precept concerning embracing ye grace belonging toward redemption stands as that by which ye Holy Spirit seriously commands all ye called toward accept ye offered grace belonging toward redemption in Christ and toward enjoy it toward their salvation. — V.

title: VI–XIII. Degrees and modes: public preaching, singular revelation, direct and indirect
latin: VI. Gradus supernae vocationis sunt, secundum quos 1. est publicae praedicationis aut singularis revelationis. VII. Publicae praedicationis est, qua gratia redemtionis toti mundo annunciatur & serio offertur, Matth. 28:19; Act. 17:30; Col. 1:28. VIII. Singularis revelationis est ordinaria aut extraordinaria. IX. Ordinaria est, qua Spiritus sanctus usus est sub V.T. in responsis ex propitiatorio & per Urim & Thummim. XI. Est directa aut indirecta. XIII. Indirecta est, qua Spiritus sanctus per media secundaria homines ad Christum ducit. Sufficiens vocatio est quae omnibus hominibus serio proponitur; abundans quae electis efficaciter applicatur.
english: VI. The degrees of heavenly calling are those according to which it is either of public preaching or of singular revelation.

VII. That of public preaching is that by which the grace of redemption is announced to the whole world and seriously offered (Matt. 28:19; Acts 17:30; Col. 1:28). VIII. Singular revelation is ordinary or extraordinary. IX. The ordinary is that which the Holy Spirit used under the Old Testament in responses from the mercy-seat and through Urim and Thummim.

XI. It is direct or indirect. XIII. Indirect is that by which the Holy Spirit leads humans to Christ through secondary means. Sufficient calling is that which is seriously proposed to all humans; abundant calling is that which is efficaciously applied to the elect.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Ye degrees belonging toward heavenly calling stand as those according toward which it stands as either belonging toward public preaching or belonging toward singular revelation. — VI. — Ye ordinary stands as that which ye Holy Spirit used under ye Old Testament in responses from ye mercy-seat and through Urim and Thummim. — IX. — Singular revelation stands as ordinary or extraordinary. — VIII. — 1:28). — Col. — Acts 17:30; — 28:19; — That belonging toward public preaching stands as that by which ye grace belonging toward redemption stands as announced toward ye whole world and seriously offered (Matt. — VII. — abundant calling stands as that which stands as efficaciously applied toward ye elect. — Sufficient calling stands as that which stands as seriously proposed toward all humans; — Indirect stands as that by which ye Holy Spirit leads humans toward Christ through secondary means. — XIII. — It stands as direct or indirect. — XI.

title: XVII–XX. Abundant, operating, preventing, and assisting grace
latin: XVII. Abundantis gratiae vocatio dicitur etiam vocatio efficax. Operans dicitur, vel quia Deus eam in homine sine ipso operatur, vel quia Deus per eam etiam solus & sine homine seu eius consensu, ut velit, operatur. Dicitur & gratia praeveniens, quia omnino praevenit humanum consensum & est auxilium, quod Deus homini in peccatis adhuc mortuo largitur, intellectum eius illuminando aut voluntatem ad actus salutares movendo. XX. Adjuvantis gratiae vocatio est, qua Spiritus sanctus hominem jam excitatum, ut velit, juvat ad bonum quod vult, ut ita loquar, volendum & perficiendum. Haec gratia in homine operatur velle, sed non sine ipso consentiente & humano more cooperante: sic tamen, ut ipsum quoque velle in divinam gratiam, tanquam in primum eius principium, in solidum referatur. Dicitur etiam comitans, consequens & cooperans.
english: XVII. The calling of abundant grace is also called efficacious calling. It is called operating either because God works it in the human without the human, or because God through it also works alone and without the human or his consent, as He wills. It is also called preventing grace, because it altogether precedes human consent and is the help that God grants to a human still dead in sins, by illuminating his intellect or moving the will to saving acts.

XX. The calling of assisting grace is that by which the Holy Spirit aids a human already excited so that he wills, toward the good that he wills — so to speak — to be willed and perfected. This grace works willing in the human, but not without him consenting and cooperating in a human manner; yet so that the willing itself also is referred wholly to divine grace as its first principle. It is also called accompanying, consequent, and cooperating.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): It stands as also called preventing grace, because it altogether precedes human consent and stands as ye help that God grants toward a human still dead in sins, by illuminating his intellect or moving ye will toward saving acts. — It stands as called operating either because God works it in ye human without ye human, or because God through it also works alone and without ye human or his consent, as He wills. — Ye calling belonging toward abundant grace stands as also called efficacious calling. — XVII. — It stands as also called accompanying, consequent, and cooperating. — yet so that ye willing itself also stands as referred wholly toward divine grace as its first principle. — This grace works willing in ye human, but not without him consenting and cooperating in a human manner; — Ye calling belonging toward assisting grace stands as that by which ye Holy Spirit aids a human already excited so that he wills, toward ye good that he wills — so toward speak — toward be willed and perfected. — XX.

title: XXI–XXIII. External and internal calling
latin: XXI. Est externa aut interna. Externa est quae fit per verbum externe praedicatum & sacramentorum administrationem. XXIII. Interna est, qua Spiritus sanctus mentem illuminat & voluntatem flectit, ut homo vocationi externa serio & efficaciter obtemperet. Haec etiam aliquando & modo quodam extraordinario sine externo verbo fieri potest, sed ordinarium Dei institutum est verbum cum interna Spiritus operatione conjungere.
english: XXI. It is external or internal. External is that which is done through the externally preached word and the administration of the sacraments.

XXIII. Internal is that by which the Holy Spirit illuminates the mind and bends the will, so that the human seriously and efficaciously obeys the external calling. This can also sometimes and in a certain extraordinary mode happen without the external word, but God's ordinary institution is to join the word with the internal operation of the Spirit.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): External stands as that which stands as done through ye externally preached word and ye administration belonging toward ye sacraments. — It stands as external or internal. — XXI. — This can also sometimes and in a certain extraordinary mode happen without ye external word, but God's ordinary institution stands as toward join ye word with ye internal operation belonging toward ye Spirit. — Internal stands as that by which ye Holy Spirit illuminates ye mind and bends ye will, so that ye human seriously and efficaciously obeys ye external calling. — XXIII.

title: XXIV–XXV. Effects of calling-grace; three notabilia
latin: XXIV. Effectus gratiae vocationis sunt illuminatio, regeneratio, fides, conversio & sanctificatio inchoata. XXV. Sunt autem hic quaedam NOTABILIA. 1. Quamvis Deus non eodem modo omnes gentes & personas vocet, nihilominus nemini deest quod ad salutem sufficeret, si non sua culpa obstaret. 2. Quod Deus externam Euangelii praedicationem aliquibus gentibus diutius subtrahat, justum eius judicium non tollit, quin serio velit omnes salvos fieri. 3. Quod non omnes vocationi obediunt, id non est culpa vocantis, sed vocatorum & diaboli.
english: XXIV. The effects of the grace of calling are illumination, regeneration, faith, conversion, and begun sanctification.

XXV. Here there are certain NOTABLE points. 1. Although God does not call all nations and persons in the same mode, nevertheless no one lacks what would suffice for salvation if his own fault did not obstruct. 2. That God withdraws the external preaching of the Gospel from some nations for a longer time does not remove His just judgment, nor that He seriously wills all to be saved. 3. That not all obey the calling is not the fault of the One who calls, but of the called and of the devil.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Ye effects belonging toward ye grace belonging toward calling stand as illumination, regeneration, faith, conversion, and begun sanctification. — XXIV. — That not all obey ye calling stands as not ye fault belonging toward ye One who calls, but belonging toward ye called and belonging toward ye devil. — 3. — That God withdraws ye external preaching belonging toward ye Gospel from some nations toward a longer time does not remove His just judgment, nor that He seriously wills all toward be saved. — 2. — Although God does not call all nations and persons in ye same mode, nevertheless no one lacks what would suffice toward salvation if his own fault did not obstruct. — 1. — Here there stand as certain NOTABLE points. — XXV.

title: Cap.6 close: why some refuse; against Pelagians; Cap.7 next on the law
latin: Id docet Christus Luc. 8:12-14; Luc. 14:18. Nam quidam prorsus audire nolunt; quidam audiunt somnolenter; alii spe utilitatis externae aut studio novitatis aut animo calumniandi; alii perpetua peccandi consuetudine semetipsos indurant; alii sapientiam & eloquentiam secularem in concionatoribus quaerunt; alii ab agnita veritate sponte sua secedunt. Plura qui volet de gratia Dei eiusque necessitate in negocio salutis contra Pelagianos veteres & novos legat cumprimis historiam Pelagianam a viris magnis Johanne Latio & Gerhardo Jo. Vossio descriptam. CAPUT SEPTIMUM sequitur, De mediis salutis humanae, & quidem nominatim de lege.
english: Christ teaches this (Luke 8:12-14; Luke 14:18). For some altogether refuse to hear; some hear sleepily; others from hope of external advantage, or zeal for novelty, or a spirit of slander; others harden themselves by perpetual habit of sinning; others seek secular wisdom and eloquence in preachers; others of their own accord withdraw from acknowledged truth.

Whoever wants more on the grace of God and its necessity in the business of salvation against old and new Pelagians should read especially the Pelagian history described by the great men Johannes Latium and Gerhard Johann Vossius.
CHAPTER SEVEN follows, On the means of human salvation, and namely on the law.
